name: Attio — testimonial-backed sales inquiry
borrow: split inquiry section with promise and attributed testimonial beside a six-field qualification form
why: The proof explains why a visitor should trust the conversation while a focused form gathers useful sales context.
fit: A consultative sale where team size and region affect the response, and a genuine customer endorsement can reduce uncertainty.
avoid: Low-commitment newsletter signup or urgent support. Qualification questions should earn their added effort.
slots: Sales context label; specific demo promise; short explanation; attributed customer quote; first and last name; work email; region; team size; needs; submit action and disclosure.
composition: Two equal-width panels separated by a hairline. The left has a large two-line headline and supporting copy above a lower testimonial. The right uses paired short fields, full-width email and details, and a dark full-width action.
mobile_behavior: The desktop split becomes intro, one-column form, then testimonial. First/last name and the qualification controls stack individually. The saved mobile capture includes the full sequence, with extra space between intro and form.
rebuild: Create a section with copy/proof and form regions. Use a two-column field grid for short controls and full spans for email and textarea. Stack the regions and fields at a content-driven breakpoint. Keep real labels, selected values, validation, and submission status in the component contract.
assets: A verified attributed quote and optional customer identity; no decorative hero asset is necessary. Use the client's actual form destination.
adapt: Tailor qualification to the sales process, shorten the empty mobile spacing, and specify the promised response or demo outcome. Move proof earlier on phones if trust is the main obstacle.
interaction: Form labels and controls were inspected; no fields were submitted and error/success states were not exercised. The mobile quote appears after the form.
verification: Live desktop/mobile inspection; full-page captures were cropped before the unrelated footer.

name: Linear — intent-routing contact cards
borrow: three contact-routing cards for sales, support, and other inquiries above a quieter self-service resource grid
why: Visitors choose their reason for contacting the company before encountering a form, reducing misrouted requests.
fit: An organization with different teams or workflows for sales, support, press, partnerships, and product help.
avoid: A small business with one inbox and one main inquiry type; routing should simplify a real distinction.
slots: Short assistance headline; two or three contact purposes; descriptions that distinguish those purposes; route labels; optional docs/community/status resources.
composition: A large left-aligned question introduces three equal dark cards. Each card separates a short title, explanatory text, and route. Lower resource links use a lighter visual hierarchy instead of competing for attention.
mobile_behavior: Sales and support become a vertical list with separators. Other inquiries moves into the resource area, rather than preserving three identical large cards. Secondary resources remain below.
rebuild: Use a semantic navigation list for primary routes and a separate resource list. Let the whole relevant route area be usable while keeping a clear accessible label. On phones reduce card chrome and preserve purpose before destination.
assets: No large imagery needed. Prepare the actual sales/support destinations and resource taxonomy.
adapt: Route by visitor intention, not internal department jargon. Limit choices to meaningful differences and keep support available without forcing a sales form.
interaction: Destination links and the inquiry email affordance were inspected; messages and forms were not submitted. External support/community journeys were not tested.
verification: Desktop/mobile captures inspected; main content retained and the unrelated footer cropped.

name: Studio Freight — editorial project brief form
borrow: a narrow serif inquiry form with underlined fields and budget context, balanced by a capabilities visual and secondary links
why: The form feels like a concise project conversation and the surrounding material provides an agency-specific point of view.
fit: A studio or consultancy qualifying substantial projects with meaningful scope and budget requirements.
avoid: Commodity service bookings or urgent mobile inquiries where placeholder-only visual cues and editorial density would add friction.
slots: Inquiry label; contact identity; company; project description; approximate budget; referral source; submit; optional capabilities link and inquiry-specific FAQ.
composition: A compact form occupies a narrow column within a much larger black canvas. Thin rules replace boxed inputs. Serif text unifies labels and navigation. A secondary column carries social links and a distinctive black-and-white capabilities preview.
mobile_behavior: The form stretches across the narrow screen, followed by the FAQ, then secondary links and capabilities content. The visual does not precede the task.
rebuild: Make the form, inquiry FAQ, and secondary resources separate modules. Use real persistent labels even if the visual treatment resembles inline prompts. Define focus, error, helper-text, and textarea expansion states before implementing underlined controls.
assets: A genuine capabilities deck or work sample can supply the supporting visual. Its source-site artwork is reference material; build a client-specific preview.
adapt: Keep only qualification questions the team uses. Separate careers, press, and collaboration routes from the project form. Use the brand's own type and voice.
interaction: Visible fields and submit control were inspected. The adjoining inquiry FAQ was opened separately. No inquiry was sent; validation and delivery remain untested.
verification: Live desktop/mobile inspection; captures show the actual form and surrounding editorial structure.

name: Stripe — staged sales-routing form
borrow: a centered white form card over a flowing branded background, with a three-step progress indicator and a two-field first stage
why: The first screen asks for little while making the remaining path explicit; the surrounding asset adds identity without entering the form.
fit: A genuine multi-stage inquiry where early answers route the visitor to a relevant next step.
avoid: Short forms split solely to make them look easier. A wizard must preserve progress and explain why later questions are needed.
slots: Brand and optional account route; progress indicator; routing headline; short explanation; work email; region; continue; clear privacy information.
composition: A generous abstract ribbon fills the background while a white rectangular card holds the task. Desktop aligns labels beside controls and highlights the current progress segment in purple. The action sits at the lower right.
mobile_behavior: The card becomes near full width; labels move above controls; the continue action becomes full width. The captured mobile design simplifies the progress display. A small horizontal scrollbar was visible and should not be copied.
rebuild: Implement a real staged form with current/completed states, back navigation, retained answers, and field validation. Keep the asset independent from the card and use a static background fallback. Announce progress semantically rather than relying on a colored line.
assets: Create a branded abstract still or lightweight motion asset with enough quiet area behind the form. Match the client's own color language.
adapt: Define routing logic before drawing the stages. Keep email and region only if they affect the path; fix mobile overflow and make the next-step expectation specific.
interaction: Only the initial stage was inspected. No email was entered or submitted, and later stages, error handling, and routing were not tested. Consent UI was dismissed before final capture.
verification: Desktop/mobile first-stage screenshots inspected. The three-step journey is visible in the design, not verified end to end.

name: Unseen Studio — scene-led direct contact
borrow: a large italic serif greeting and direct email over a softly lit authored interior scene, with business/general inquiry selectors
why: The art-directed environment communicates the studio's craft while the email remains a prominent actionable element.
fit: A creative practice selling distinctive visual judgment and working through direct conversations rather than structured qualification.
avoid: Urgent service inquiries, weak devices without a fallback, or tasks where an entrance screen delays an essential action.
slots: Greeting; short invitation; business/general selector; visible direct contact; optional location details and restrained navigation.
composition: A pastel interior with curtains, a sculptural chair, platform, and reflective floor fills the view. Italic serif display type contrasts with plain interface text. The contact cluster occupies a deliberately quiet area of the scene.
mobile_behavior: The greeting, invitation, selector row, and email stack above the recropped interior. The scene retains the chair and platform at a smaller scale. The final mobile capture was taken after the entrance and typography transitions settled.
rebuild: Start with a still composition and semantic contact content. Add selector state only if it changes a real destination. Place the scene behind readable HTML and independently art-direct the mobile crop. If adding 3D or motion, preserve a fast static path.
assets: Commission, generate, or build an original brand environment with clear text-safe space. The precise source rendering technique was not verified; a Three.js runtime is not required to reproduce the compositional idea.
adapt: Borrow the relationship of an authored scene and a direct invitation. Use the client's own environment and type. Remove an entrance gate for task-focused client sites and keep email legible during any transition.
interaction: The no-audio entry was exercised and the general inquiry selector was clicked. No email client was launched. Complete selector routing, keyboard access, and reduced-motion behavior were not verified.
verification: Settled desktop/mobile viewport captures inspected. The source's entrance and animated transitions are documented as implementation considerations.

name: KUBE Saint-Tropez — map and direct contact
borrow: an equal-width map and contact-details split with a serif title and clearly separated address, phone, and email roles
why: Location and ways to reach the team are presented together, without making visitors complete a form to ask a practical question.
fit: A place-based business where finding the location and contacting staff are the main tasks.
avoid: Remote services without a visitor-facing premises; a decorative map adds cost without helping a real task.
slots: Context label; contact heading; short explanation; address; tap-to-call phone; email; map/directions; optional arrival guidance below.
composition: A large map occupies the left half and an off-white information panel the right. A constrained copy column and small uppercase field labels keep the address and channels distinct. The rest of the site supplies the visual identity.
mobile_behavior: Contact information leads and the map follows, reversing the desktop left-to-right visual order. The map has an external open-in-maps affordance. The captured iframe was still resolving map tiles on mobile.
rebuild: Use a semantic address/contact region and a separate map region. Set the mobile reading order intentionally; keep essential details outside the iframe. Provide a direct directions link and a static or lazy-loaded map alternative.
assets: Use the actual location and map provider appropriate to the client. Include accurate coordinates, address, phone formatting, and contact destination.
adapt: Add opening hours or parking guidance if they answer common questions. Keep map embeds from consuming the mobile page before the contact channels appear.
interaction: Phone/email link destinations and the map affordance were inspected; no call, email, map navigation, or location permission was triggered.
verification: Desktop/mobile viewport captures inspected. Essential details remained readable while map imagery loaded.

name: Studio Freight — inquiry-routing FAQ
borrow: a narrow serif FAQ below the project form, routing careers, press, and collaboration requests through expandable answers
why: The questions sort different kinds of correspondence without adding those choices to the main project form.
fit: A project inquiry page receiving several kinds of non-client correspondence.
avoid: A general product help center or a large corpus of technical questions; the narrow editorial column suits a small set.
slots: FAQ label; inquiry-type questions; short answers; appropriate contact links; optional brand-personality questions.
composition: A narrow list of underlined rows shares the form's serif typography. Right-aligned plus controls change to a cross for the expanded answer. The answer stays within the same column.
mobile_behavior: The list expands to the screen's available width below the form. Answers wrap into short lines; secondary links and capabilities content follow. The capture shows the careers answer expanded.
rebuild: Use accessible accordion buttons inside headings with controlled answer regions. Keep the inquiry links as actual anchors. Define active icon, row divider, focus, answer spacing, and long-email wrapping.
assets: No imagery is needed inside the FAQ. The adjacent capabilities preview belongs to the surrounding contact page.
adapt: Use real correspondence categories. A small personality question can fit an agency voice, but place operational questions first. Improve heading and button semantics if the source's paragraph-based appearance is reused.
interaction: The careers row was clicked and its answer became visible with a changed indicator. Email links were inspected but not launched; keyboard behavior was not tested.
verification: Expanded-state desktop/mobile captures inspected; this is an inquiry FAQ rather than a purchase-objection list.

name: KUBE Saint-Tropez — editorial practical FAQ
borrow: wide ruled question rows beneath a left-aligned serif heading, with small lime plus/minus controls and one active answer
why: The section keeps practical questions scan-friendly while retaining the hospitality site's editorial character.
fit: Practical access, appointment, arrival, and service questions near a contact or booking decision.
avoid: Long policy documents or situations where critical restrictions would be hidden from purchasers.
slots: Context label; FAQ heading; approximately six distinct practical questions; concise answers with relevant links.
composition: An off-white canvas, generous row spacing, thin dividers, uppercase question labels, and lime circular toggles. Answers occupy a narrower measure than the full question row.
mobile_behavior: Questions wrap while the toggle stays at the right edge. The answer remains in the same vertical flow. The saved mobile state shows the address answer open.
rebuild: Build a single-open accordion with heading/button pairs and explicit expanded states. Reserve space for the toggle; constrain answer measure independently from the question row. Make the full question usable as the control.
assets: No section-specific imagery; use the brand's type and accent roles. Any adjacent photographs should be real client material.
adapt: Use actual visitor questions and retain essential booking terms elsewhere in visible content. Keep desktop rows from becoming unnecessarily tall on phones.
interaction: The address question was clicked; the previous answer collapsed and the selected one opened. Keyboard navigation and every answer were not tested.
verification: Live desktop/mobile expanded-state captures inspected. The desktop heading is partly behind the persistent header in the saved view; its full treatment is visible on mobile.

name: Raycast Pro — centered dark accordion
borrow: a centered section title above a constrained accordion column with bold questions, dimmer answers, and simple chevrons
why: Clear type hierarchy and a readable answer width make a potentially dense product FAQ feel controlled.
fit: A product or subscription page with a handful of real buying objections and moderate answer lengths.
avoid: Many unrelated support issues or long answers that dominate the narrow mobile screen.
slots: Section title; brief contextual line; question buttons; plain-language answers; relevant detail links.
composition: Near-black background, large centered introduction, then a narrower question list. Bold white questions and gray body text separate scanning from reading. Hairline separators and chevrons supply state cues.
mobile_behavior: The constrained column fills the available width. Questions and answers wrap naturally; the long expanded answer occupies much of the captured phone screen.
rebuild: Use a shared container and narrower answer column. Implement real buttons, expanded state, answer regions, visible focus, and collapse/open behavior. Choose answer lengths before setting vertical spacing.
assets: Typography and spacing carry the section; no images are required.
adapt: Shorten long answers and link to detail pages. Check the contrast of secondary text rather than blindly reproducing dim gray. Replace all provider, plan, and privacy claims with verified client facts.
interaction: The first privacy question was opened, collapsed, and reopened during desktop/mobile inspection. Expanded state appeared in the accessibility snapshot. No linked workflows were completed.
verification: Desktop/mobile screenshots of the expanded accordion were inspected; product claims are source content, not recommendations or reusable copy.

name: Framer — always-visible pricing answers
borrow: an open question-and-answer list in a narrow centered column, using spacing rather than accordion controls to separate answers
why: Visitors can read and search pricing explanations without opening individual rows.
fit: A manageable set of concise pricing explanations that should remain visible together.
avoid: Dozens of lengthy answers or a page already too long to scan.
slots: FAQ heading; question headings; direct answers; useful account, plan, or support links.
composition: Black background and centered section heading precede a narrow left-aligned text column. Each question is brighter than its answer; generous vertical separation replaces boxed cards and toggles.
mobile_behavior: The content becomes a padded single column with all answers visible. Lines wrap without introducing extra controls or interaction.
rebuild: Use semantic question headings and ordinary answer content. Set a readable maximum width, an explicit question-to-answer gap, and a larger gap between entries. Keep links distinguishable and long pricing terms readable.
assets: No section imagery. The design depends on accurate concise copy and disciplined type sizing.
adapt: Choose this pattern when disclosure is more useful than compression. Group or add a table of contents if the answer count grows; preserve important purchase conditions outside any later accordion redesign.
interaction: The answers were visible without clicks on desktop and mobile. Pricing, billing, and support destinations were not exercised.
verification: Desktop/mobile layout inspected. A fading consent panel remains at the edge of the desktop capture and does not cover the answer column.

name: Switchyards — topic-linked document FAQ
borrow: a large editorial FAQ title with pill-shaped topic jump links above a long, always-visible question-and-answer document
why: Topic navigation makes a substantial FAQ usable without hiding the answers, and the typography preserves the brand's character.
fit: Membership or venue information covering several distinct practical themes.
avoid: A short three-question section where a full topic index adds unnecessary interface.
slots: FAQ title; topic index; category headings; question headings; direct answers; links; return-to-top control.
composition: A warm light background and navy editorial type. A centered title sits over a row of thin outlined topic pills. Large category headings and smaller question headings create a document hierarchy.
mobile_behavior: Topic pills wrap across several rows and the document becomes a padded single column. The visual hierarchy stays intact rather than collapsing into an unrelated help-center template.
rebuild: Create a linked topic index and semantic sections with stable IDs. Use scroll margins to keep anchored headings clear of sticky navigation. Add a return-to-top route and preserve browser hash navigation.
assets: No major visual assets; a carefully chosen serif and optional small brand marks supply character.
adapt: Organize by visitor questions rather than department names. Reduce excessive heading whitespace if mobile readers must reach answers quickly. Use a more readable body face if long serif answers slow scanning.
interaction: The Phone Booths jump link was exercised and the URL changed to its category anchor. The complete document remained open. All category links and keyboard navigation were not tested.
verification: Desktop/mobile captures inspected; a transient viewport-scaling capture was replaced with a settled phone view.

name: TypeSafe AI — terminal-inspired technical accordion
borrow: monospace question labels and small square arrow controls paired with large sans-serif answers and a thin vertical rule
why: The contrast between terminal-like controls and readable answer text creates a distinctive technical voice without requiring decorative images.
fit: A technically fluent audience evaluating mechanism, reliability, or integration questions.
avoid: Brands whose audience would find terminal conventions unfamiliar, or layouts where uppercase monospace labels become difficult to read.
slots: Section title; technical questions; square state controls; plain-language answer paragraphs; appropriate detail links.
composition: Dark gray canvas with bracket-like details. Questions occupy a narrower left-side column with a vertical line and sparse square controls. Answers switch to larger sans-serif text with clear paragraph breaks.
mobile_behavior: The same accordion becomes full width with wrapping monospace questions. Large answer text can occupy an entire screen; the saved phone capture shows an expanded second answer.
rebuild: Implement accessible question buttons and answer regions first, then add line and bracket decoration. Keep the answer readable at narrow widths, preserve focus visibility, and ensure icon direction consistently conveys expanded state.
assets: Mostly CSS typography and simple vector lines. No generated scene or large image is required.
adapt: Borrow the mixed typography and schematic control grammar. Keep claims specific to the client and shorten answers where a large mobile type size creates excessive scrolling.
interaction: The second question was clicked and its answer opened while the previous answer closed. Expanded button state was present in the loaded snapshot. Full keyboard and reduced-motion behavior were not tested.
verification: Desktop/mobile expanded-state captures inspected. A loading overlay in the first mobile attempt was replaced with a settled capture.

name: KUBE Saint-Tropez — restrained reservation close
borrow: a centered serif invitation and one lime booking button in a quiet band immediately before the footer
why: A clear action and generous separation let the visitor act after practical questions have been answered.
fit: A page that has already established the offer and resolved objections, leaving one obvious next step.
avoid: A cold visitor who still needs to understand the product or choose among several different services.
slots: Small context label; concise invitation; booking action; optional expectation or reassurance when required.
composition: Warm off-white band, centered serif display line, and a small contrasting lime button. A divider separates the closing invitation from the utility footer.
mobile_behavior: The headline wraps into a compact two-line block. The booking button expands to nearly the available width, preserving its prominence.
rebuild: Build a semantic CTA region with one action, consistent section padding, and bounded text width. Make the mobile control comfortably usable and keep any booking integration out of the initial page load when practical.
assets: No new imagery is needed; the surrounding page carries the destination's visual world.
adapt: Make the action describe the actual next step. Add availability or response expectations only when accurate. Preserve this restrained option for pages whose imagery is already rich.
interaction: The booking control was observed. No booking was submitted; the external booking engine and transaction journey were not tested.
verification: Desktop/mobile viewport screenshots inspected; this is a visual and clarity reference rather than measured conversion evidence.

name: Switchyards — membership offer and oversized join action
borrow: an editorial price promise beside two billing choices inside one panel, anchored by a full-width pill-shaped join button
why: The offer and its billing distinction sit immediately next to one decisive action instead of dispersing the decision across several cards.
fit: One membership with a small number of billing choices and a clear entry path.
avoid: Complex feature-tier comparisons or offers where the displayed periodic price conceals a larger commitment.
slots: Offer headline; actual billing choices; price and period; transparent commitment terms; optional truthful savings cue; join action.
composition: A large navy serif promise fills the left column. The right is a pale rounded panel with two price groups, small branded stickers, and an oversized navy action spanning the panel.
mobile_behavior: The promise sits above the offer panel. Prices remain grouped and the large join control stays within the panel. The narrow layout preserves the brand's serif character and navy contrast.
rebuild: Use an offer-summary region and an adjacent conversion panel. Represent each billing option semantically and keep period/commitment next to the value. Stack the two regions on small screens and retain a clear dominant action.
assets: Optional small custom badge illustrations; they should reinforce a real offer rather than simulate urgency.
adapt: Use this for the client's actual offer. Show total commitment and savings honestly. If plans differ in substance, introduce a comparison rather than forcing them into this compact format.
interaction: Join and membership destinations were observed; no membership was purchased, no location permission was requested, and checkout was not exercised.
verification: Desktop/mobile captures inspected. Source prices and savings are contextual evidence, not reusable client claims.

name: Linear — self-service and sales closing CTA
borrow: a compact two-line promise above a bright self-service action and quieter sales action, separated from the footer by ample space
why: The hierarchy accommodates both ready-to-start users and buyers who need a conversation.
fit: A product with genuinely useful self-service and assisted-sales entry points.
avoid: A campaign with one intended destination, where a second action would dilute the decision.
slots: Short closing promise; primary start action; secondary sales action; optional relevant reassurance.
composition: Near-black section, narrow centered white headline, and two adjacent pill controls. The bright primary action contrasts with the darker secondary action; the rest of the band stays quiet.
mobile_behavior: The headline wraps more tightly while both actions remain together in the captured phone width. The footer follows after a visible separation.
rebuild: Create a CTA group with a clear primary/secondary style relationship. Allow controls to wrap or stack before labels become cramped. Keep spacing between the CTA region and footer independent from button layout.
assets: No section-specific media; typography and action contrast do the work.
adapt: Change the promise and button labels to match the client journey. Keep the secondary route only if it serves a distinct buyer need.
interaction: Signup and contact-sales destinations were inspected. Registration and inquiry submission were not performed.
verification: Desktop/mobile captures inspected. The minimalist treatment provides a useful contrast to more asset-heavy options.

name: Framer — product-start CTA with a mobile alternative
borrow: an inline prompt composer beneath the closing headline on desktop, replaced by a direct signup button and glowing product visual on mobile
why: Desktop lets the visitor begin the product task immediately, while mobile offers a simpler commitment and a focused visual.
fit: A product whose first meaningful action can be initiated in a small inline interaction.
avoid: A simulated composer with no actual continuation, or an interaction that asks for sensitive project details before explaining handling.
slots: Closing headline; desktop input/composer and submit affordance; helpful starting suggestions; alternative start path; mobile button; product visual.
composition: Centered white headline above a dark rectangular composer. Suggested use cases and an alternate route sit below. The desktop interface is itself the central visual.
mobile_behavior: The composer and suggestion chips are replaced by a prominent start button and a glowing cropped canvas UI image. This is an observed change of interaction, not simply a smaller desktop box.
rebuild: Build separate responsive presentations of the same intended journey. On desktop, carry the user's input into a real product flow. On mobile, route directly and use a compact accurate visual. Keep accessible labels and loading/error states explicit.
assets: An accurate product-interface crop with a controlled glow treatment for the mobile presentation. Use the client's own UI and keep actual controls as HTML.
adapt: Only embed the task if it can continue without losing input. Decide which devices benefit from it; use a normal CTA elsewhere. Keep an accessible non-composer route available.
interaction: The composer, suggested prompts, mobile replacement, and destinations were inspected. No prompt was submitted and continuation, signup, or generation was not tested.
verification: Desktop/mobile captures show a deliberate change of content and interaction at the narrow viewport.

name: Front — branded demo panel with people imagery
borrow: a large inset deep-purple CTA panel with a left-aligned white promise, lime demo button, and supporting people imagery
why: A strong color field and contrasting action create a recognizable closing destination after a long product story.
fit: An assisted-sale offer that needs a distinctive final invitation and credible human context.
avoid: Pages where additional chat widgets or competing CTAs obscure the main action.
slots: Specific outcome headline; demo action; optional relevant people or workplace image; clear onward journey.
composition: Rounded inset purple panel, large left-aligned white type, and a bright lime action. The settled desktop capture includes workplace imagery at the right and a block-like branded motif below.
mobile_behavior: The message becomes a tall text block and the action remains below it. An automatically opened chat panel overlaps much of the lower section in the observed phone view, though the main button remains visible.
rebuild: Use a two-column panel when imagery helps, with separate text and image regions and a consistent inset. Stack or remove imagery on narrow screens. Design chat and floating utilities around a reserved safe area rather than letting them compete with the CTA.
assets: Licensed or client-supplied workplace photography with a focal crop that supports the message. Avoid implying stock subjects are the client's employees.
adapt: Borrow the clear color/action contrast and inset composition. Keep the promise concise and prevent automatic overlays from covering content or controls.
interaction: The demo control and chat overlay were observed. The third-party panel did not expose a usable dismissal control through the available inspection route. No chat message or demo request was submitted.
verification: Desktop/mobile captures preserve the actual overlay limitation; the rebuild should improve that behavior. The desktop photo loaded after the initial observation.

name: charity: water — illustrated newsletter signup
borrow: a small envelope illustration and benefit statement beside a signup form, with a wide yellow subscription action
why: A recognizable illustration connects the section to receiving updates while the split layout gives the form a clear place.
fit: An organization with a meaningful email program and enough reason for visitors to stay connected.
avoid: A generic newsletter request without a clear benefit, or unnecessary personal questions that add effort without relevance.
slots: Small illustration; useful signup promise; brief description; email and justified identity fields; optional preference; subscription action; clear information-use note.
composition: A white signup panel on a warm pale surround. The left combines envelope artwork with a short headline; the right contains paired name fields, email, optional birthday controls, and the yellow action.
mobile_behavior: Illustration and invitation lead, then the fields stack. Name inputs become separate rows and birthday controls rearrange across two rows. The full-width subscription control stays in the form; a second view shows the lower context.
rebuild: Use copy/illustration and form regions in a shared panel. Keep labels persistent and required/optional states clear. Handle validation and success without losing entered values. Use a single-column layout before controls become cramped.
assets: An original small illustration matching the client's icon/line/color language; avoid copying the source envelope.
adapt: Begin with email-only unless extra fields have a concrete purpose. Make the email benefit and expected cadence specific. Explain any optional preference and preserve a clear unsubscribe path.
interaction: Fields and the subscription control were inspected; no information was entered and no subscription was sent. Consent UI was dismissed before capture; delivery, validation, and success were not tested.
verification: Desktop and complementary mobile captures inspected. The longer form is a design choice to assess, not a universal signup template.
